title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is seeing a mix of new partnerships and funding, with a notable focus on defense applications. Meanwhile, budget allocations hint at a growing recognition of the need for space resilience and data infrastructure.

themes.title: Defense Partnerships on the Rise
themes.body: Spire's collaboration with a German defense firm for missile warning systems underscores the increasing military interest in space-based capabilities. Similarly, Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for tactical satellite constellations, reflecting a trend towards integrated defense solutions.

themes.title: Funding Fuels Space Ventures
themes.body: True Anomaly's $190 million Series C round and Orbital's $5 million raise indicate that investors are still keen on space startups, particularly those with data-centric offerings. Iceye's valuation jump to 10 billion euros further illustrates the market's appetite for innovative space solutions.

themes.title: Budget Boosts for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adding $1.4 billion for space resilience highlights a governmental shift towards prioritizing security in the orbital environment. This increased funding aligns with the Space Force's plans for a robust data network backbone, emphasizing the importance of infrastructure.

themes.title: New Players Entering the Market
themes.body: UK startup Applied Atomics is making its move into the U.S. military space mobility sector, indicating a competitive landscape ahead. Additionally, the Commercial Space Federation's new members signal an expanding supply chain that could reshape industry dynamics.
